1	# Real-world Event Decision Simulator
2	
3	A small backend foundation for an emergency-response and logistics decision simulation platform. The service exposes a public HTTP entry point that future features can extend without changing the startup contract.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m event_sim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	Check the public health endpoint:
14	
15	```bash
16	curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
17	```
18	
19	## Test
20	
21	```bash
22	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	## Public interface
26	
27	- `GET /health` returns JSON with the service name and `ok` status, under the keys `service` and `status`: `{"service": "real-world-event-decision-sim", "status": "ok"}`.
28	- Unknown paths return a JSON `not_found` error with HTTP 404.
29	- `python -m event_sim --help` documents the command-line entry point.
30	
31	## Credentials and organization isolation
32	
33	Every entry point except `GET /health` and the credential registration entry
34	point requires a request-scoped Bearer credential. Credentials are held only
35	in the server process: restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with an
36	empty credential registry, and an unregistered token reaches nothing.
37	
38	### `POST /auth/tokens`
39	
40	The one entry point that requires no credential. Requires
41	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with exactly
42	these three fields, in any order:
43	
44	| Field            | Rule                                  |
45	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
46	| `token`          | non-empty string                      |
47	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                      |
48	| `role`           | one of `read` or `write`              |
49	
50	- `201 Created` — new token registered. The body echoes the three fields as
51	  compact JSON with keys sorted by code point and one trailing newline:
52	  `{"organizationId":"org-1","role":"write","token":"tok-1"}\n`.
53	- `200 OK` — the same token was resubmitted with the identical organization
54	  and role; it is not registered a second time and the same body is echoed.
55	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "auth_conflict"}`) — the token is already bound
56	  to a different organization or role. The binding is never rewritten.
57	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
58	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
59	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
60	  missing/extra field, a blank or non-string `token`/`organizationId`, or a
61	  `role` other than `read`/`write`. No record is stored.
62	
63	```bash
64	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/tokens \
65	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
66	  -d '{"token":"tok-1","organizationId":"org-1","role":"write"}'
67	```
68	
69	### Bearer authentication
70	
71	All other requests carry the registered token in an
72	`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. A missing header, a non-Bearer
73	scheme, a malformed bearer value, or an unregistered token yields
74	`401 Unauthorized` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.
75	
76	A valid credential that acts outside its bound organization or role yields
77	`403 Forbidden` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and performs no write. The
78	`organizationId` in any request parameter or body field must equal the
79	token's registered organization; reading or writing another organization's
80	data is forbidden.
81	
82	- A `read` token may call only the state-free query and decision-computation
83	  entry points: the event list, aggregate, region, and replay (including
84	  replay comparison) queries, the reservation/alert listings,
85	  `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources`,
86	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources`,
87	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/reservations`,
88	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events`,
89	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/aggregate`,
90	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/region/aggregate`,
91	  `POST /decisions/evaluate`, `POST /decisions/allocate`,
92	  `POST /branches/compare`, `POST /branches/compare/events`,
93	  `POST /branches/compare/reservations`,
94	  `POST /branches/compare/resources`, `POST /snapshots/compare`,
95	  `POST /snapshots/compare/events`,
96	  `POST /snapshots/compare/reservations`,
97	  `POST /snapshots/compare/resources`, and the other
98	  read-only branch entry points.
99	- Committing an event or reservation, evaluating an alert, and creating a
100	  snapshot or branch are writes; only a `write` token may call them. A
101	  `read` token against a write entry point receives `403`. The authorization
102	  decision and the ledger/inventory mutation complete under one lock, so a
103	  rejected request never changes the ledger or inventory.
104	
105	Snapshots and branches belong to the organization that created them. A
106	snapshot captures only that organization's events, resource capacities, and
107	reservations, and the three summary counts count only that organization; a
108	branch forks only a snapshot owned by the same organization, and branch entry
109	points authenticate with the same rules as the main service. Snapshot and
110	branch names are unique across the whole service (not merely within one
111	organization), and accessing another organization's snapshot or branch by name
112	is `403`, never `404`.
113	
114	## Event ledger
115	
116	Events are held only in the server process: restarting (or starting a new
117	instance) begins with an empty ledger.
118	
119	### `POST /events`
120	
121	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with
122	exactly these five top-level fields:
123	
124	| Field          | Rule                                      |
125	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
126	| `eventId`      | non-empty string                          |
127	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                        |
128	| `type`         | non-empty string                          |
129	| `occurredAt`   | non-negative integer (no floats, no booleans) |
130	| `payload`      | JSON object                               |
131	
132	```bash
133	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/events \
134	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
135	  -d '{"eventId":"evt-1","organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","occurredAt":100,"payload":{"severity":"low"}}'
136	```
137	
138	- `201 Created` — new event stored; the response is the same five-field JSON.
139	- `200 OK` — the same `eventId` was resubmitted with identical fields; the
140	  stored event is returned and nothing is added.
141	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "event_id_conflict"}`) — the `eventId` exists but
142	  the other fields differ.
143	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
144	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
145	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — fields are missing, extra, or invalid
146	  (arrays at the top level, blank identifiers, floats, etc.).
147	
148	### `GET /events?organizationId=...`
149	
150	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
151	Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
152	belong only to that organization and are sorted by `occurredAt`, then
153	`eventId`. An unknown organization returns `"events": []`. A missing, blank, or
154	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
155	
156	### `GET /events/aggregate?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
157	
158	Counts stored events per time window, without modifying the ledger. Only
159	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted; other
160	organizations' data is never included.
161	
162	Query parameters:
163	
164	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
165	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
166	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
167	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
168	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
169	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
170	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
171	
172	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
173	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, or invalid parameter yields
174	`422` with a JSON body containing a stable `error` field.
175	
176	Windows start at `0` and each covers `[start, end)` with
177	`end = start + windowSize`; an event belongs to a window when
178	`start <= occurredAt < end`. The `200` response is:
179	
180	```json
181	{
182	  "organizationId": "org-1",
183	  "type": "incident.created",
184	  "windowSize": 60,
185	  "from": null,
186	  "to": null,
187	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
188	}
189	```
190	
191	- Without `from`/`to` (`from` and `to` echo back as `null`), only windows
192	  actually covered by matching events are returned; with no matching events
193	  `windows` is `[]`.
194	- With `from`/`to`, only events with `from <= occurredAt <= to` are counted,
195	  and every window intersecting the closed interval `[from, to]` is returned,
196	  including empty windows with `count: 0`.
197	- `windows` is sorted by `start` ascending; results are deterministic
198	  regardless of event insertion order, replays, or identical timestamps.
199	
200	```bash
201	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
202	```
203	
204	### Region attribution
205	
206	An event's region is the value of the `region` key in its `payload`. Only a
207	non-empty string attributes an event to a region: a missing key, an empty
208	string, or a non-string value means the event has no region. Region values
209	are matched verbatim (exact comparison, no trimming or normalization), and
210	regions need no registration — an unknown region simply matches zero events
211	and is never implicitly created. The region endpoints below are read-only:
212	they never write the event ledger, reservations, or alerts.
213	
214	### `GET /events/region?organizationId=...&region=...`
215	
216	Lists one organization's events attributed to one region. Both
217	`organizationId` and `region` must appear exactly once and be non-empty; a
218	missing, duplicated, or blank parameter yields `422`. Returns `200` with
219	`{"organizationId": "...", "region": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
220	are sorted by `occurredAt`, then `eventId`, exactly like `GET /events`. An
221	unknown organization or region returns `"events": []`; other organizations'
222	events are never included. The body is compact JSON with keys sorted by code
223	point and a trailing newline.
224	
225	```bash
226	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region?organizationId=org-1&region=north'
227	```

229	### `GET /events/region/aggregate?organizationId=...&region=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
230	
231	Counts per time window, using the exact same parameter rules, window
232	boundaries, ordering, and `from`/`to` semantics as
233	`GET /events/aggregate`, with an added `region` parameter that must appear
234	exactly once and be non-empty. Only events matching the organization,
235	region, and type are counted; events without a non-empty string payload
236	`region` never match. The `200` response mirrors the aggregate response with
237	one added `region` key (compact JSON, keys sorted by code point, trailing
238	newline):
239	
240	```json
241	{
242	  "organizationId": "org-1",
243	  "region": "north",
244	  "type": "incident.created",
245	  "windowSize": 60,
246	  "from": null,
247	  "to": null,
248	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
249	}
250	```
251	
252	Without a range, only windows covered by matching events are returned; an
253	unknown region behaves like a zero-event match. With a range, every window
254	intersecting `[from, to]` is returned, including empty ones. Any parameter
255	problem — missing, duplicated, or blank values, a non-positive-integer
256	`windowSize`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to` — yields
257	`422` with `{"error": "validation_error", ...}`.
258	
259	```bash
260	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&region=north&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
261	```
262	
263	### `POST /decisions/evaluate`
264	
265	A read-only, deterministic emergency decision over the same windows as the
266	aggregate endpoint. The ledger is never written to or changed by a decision
267	request. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON
268	object containing exactly these fields:
269	
270	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
271	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
272	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
273	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
274	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
275	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
276	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
277	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
278	
279	Only events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted. Windows
280	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`. Without `from`/`to`,
281	only windows actually covered by matching events are considered; with a
282	range, events are filtered by the closed interval `from <= occurredAt <= to`
283	and every window intersecting that interval is considered, including empty
284	ones for audit reconciliation.
285	
286	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
287	
288	```json
289	{
290	  "organizationId": "org-1",
291	  "type": "incident.created",
292	  "windowSize": 60,
293	  "from": null,
294	  "to": null,
295	  "peakStart": 60,
296	  "peakCount": 2,
297	  "action": "observe"
298	}
299	```
300	
301	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
302	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
303	  regardless of event submission order.
304	- With no matching events (or no non-empty windows in range), `peakCount` is
305	  `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and `action` is `"observe"`.
306	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
307	  `"observe"`.
308	- Unknown organizations or types compute as zero events and return normally;
309	  other organizations' data is never included.
310	
311	```bash
312	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/evaluate \
313	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
314	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
315	```
316	
317	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
318	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no decision is
319	  produced.
320	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
321	  invalid types, unpaired `from`/`to`, or out-of-range values.
322	
323	### `POST /decisions/allocate`
324	
325	A read-only, deterministic resource plan computed entirely from the request
326	body. Nothing is written to the event ledger, no earlier plan is inherited,
327	and concurrent requests cannot affect each other. Requires
328	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object containing
329	exactly these fields:
330	
331	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
332	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
333	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
334	| `demands`        | required array (may be empty) of demand objects              |
335	| `resources`      | required array (may be empty) of resource objects            |
336	
337	A demand object has exactly `demandId` (non-empty string, unique within the
338	request), `units` (positive integer), and `priority` (non-negative integer).
339	A resource object has exactly `resourceId` (non-empty string, unique within
340	the request) and `capacity` (positive integer). Booleans, floats, negative or
341	zero values where a positive integer is required, wrong element types, blank
342	or duplicate identifiers, and unknown fields are all rejected.
343	
344	Demands are handled by `priority` descending; ties resolve by `demandId` in
345	Unicode code-point order. A demand is placed wholly into the
346	lexicographically smallest `resourceId` whose remaining capacity covers its
347	units, and that capacity is deducted immediately. Demands are never split and
348	capacity is never oversold; a demand that fits in no remaining resource goes
349	to `unassigned` — priorities and units are never adjusted to place more
350	demands.
351	
352	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
353	
354	```json
355	{
356	  "organizationId": "org-1",
357	  "assignments": [
358	    {"demandId": "d-a", "resourceId": "r-a", "units": 2},
359	    {"demandId": "d-b", "resourceId": "r-b", "units": 4}
360	  ],
361	  "unassigned": ["d-big"],
362	  "totalUnits": 6
363	}
364	```
365	
366	- `assignments` lists `{"demandId", "resourceId", "units"}` objects in
367	  processing order.
368	- `unassigned` lists the demandIds that could not be placed, sorted by
369	  `demandId`.
370	- `totalUnits` counts only units that were assigned.
371	- Empty `demands`/`resources` arrays are valid and return empty results;
372	  identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
373	
374	```bash
375	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/allocate \
376	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
377	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","demands":[{"demandId":"d-a","units":2,"priority":1}],"resources":[{"resourceId":"r-a","capacity":5}]}'
378	```
379	
380	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
381	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
382	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
383	  invalid types, duplicate or blank identifiers, or out-of-range values.
384	
385	## Reservation inventory
386	
387	Reservations are held only in the server process alongside the event ledger:
388	restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with empty inventory. The
389	first reservation that names a resource fixes that resource's capacity; it
390	is never rewritten afterwards.
391	
392	### `POST /reservations`
393	
394	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
395	with exactly these five top-level fields:
396	
397	| Field           | Rule                                      |
398	| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
399	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                         |
400	| `reservationId` | non-empty string                          |
401	| `resourceId`    | non-empty string                          |
402	| `quantity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
403	| `capacity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
404	
405	```bash
406	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reservations \
407	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
408	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a","quantity":2,"capacity":5}'
409	```
410	
411	A successful response is compact JSON with stable key order, integer values,
412	and a trailing newline:
413	
414	```json
415	{"capacity":5,"occupied":2,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":2,"remaining":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a"}
416	```
417	
418	`occupied` is the total confirmed quantity on the resource and `remaining`
419	is `capacity - occupied`; the balance can never go negative because the
420	check and the deduction commit atomically under one lock, so concurrent
421	requests cannot oversell a resource or lose each other's writes.
422	
423	- `201 Created` — new reservation committed; the first reservation for a
424	  resource also establishes its capacity.
425	- `200 OK` — the same `reservationId` was resubmitted with identical fields;
426	  nothing is counted twice and the balances are unchanged.
427	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "reservation_conflict"}`) — the `reservationId`
428	  exists but the other fields differ.
429	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_conflict"}`) — the resource already
430	  has a recorded capacity and the declared `capacity` differs; the recorded
431	  capacity is never rewritten.
432	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_exceeded"}`) — the quantity exceeds
433	  the resource's remaining balance; inventory and existing reservations are
434	  unchanged.
435	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
436	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no reservation
437	  is produced.
438	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
439	  blank or non-string identifiers, or non-positive/non-integer values.
440	
441	### `GET /reservations?organizationId=...`
442	
443	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
444	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "reservations":
445	[...]}` containing only that organization's reservations, sorted by
446	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each entry
447	carries `quantity`, the resource's `capacity`, and the resource-wide
448	`occupied` and `remaining` balances. An unknown organization returns
449	`"reservations": []`. A missing, blank, or duplicated parameter yields
450	`422`.

452	## Alert suppression and escalation
453	
454	Alerts are held only in the main service process alongside the event
455	ledger; restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with no alerts.
456	Snapshots and branches never capture alerts, and the alert entry points
457	exist only on the main service — no `/branches/{branchId}/alerts/...`
458	paths are added.
459	
460	### `POST /alerts/evaluate`
461	
462	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
463	containing exactly these fields:
464	
465	| Field               | Rule                                                          |
466	| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
467	| `organizationId`    | required, non-empty string                                   |
468	| `type`              | required, non-empty string                                   |
469	| `windowSize`        | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
470	| `threshold`         | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
471	| `suppressionWindow` | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
472	| `from`              | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
473	| `to`                | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
474	
475	The peak uses the exact same windowing as `POST /decisions/evaluate`: only
476	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted, windows
477	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`, ties resolve to the
478	earliest window start, and an unknown organization or type computes as
479	zero events. The event ledger is never modified.
480	
481	- When the peak is below the threshold, `action` is `"observe"`, no alert
482	  is written, `alertId` is `null`, and `suppressedCount` is `null`.
483	- When the peak reaches the threshold, the peak start is compared with the
484	  most recent prior alert for the same organization and type:
485	  - `peakStart` not earlier than the prior start and at least
486	    `suppressionWindow` away (`peakStart - priorStart >=
487	    suppressionWindow`) creates a new alert; `action` is `"escalate"`,
488	    `alertId` is the new id (`alert-1`, `alert-2`, …, one global sequence
489	    across all organizations and types), and `suppressedCount` is `0`.
490	  - A peak start less than `suppressionWindow` after the prior alert's
491	    peak start increments that alert's suppression count instead; `action`
492	    is `"suppress"`, `alertId` is the prior alert's id, and
493	    `suppressedCount` is the new total. The first threshold hit for an
494	    organization/type always creates an alert.
495	
496	The suppression decision and the alert creation commit atomically under
497	one lock, so concurrent threshold hits cannot both open alerts or suppress
498	against a stale view. The `200` response echoes every request parameter
499	and adds the result fields (compact JSON, stable key order, integer values,
500	trailing newline):
501	
502	```json
503	{"action":"escalate","alertId":"alert-1","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60,"suppressedCount":0,"suppressionWindow":120,"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
504	```
505	
506	```bash
507	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/alerts/evaluate \
508	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
509	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3,"suppressionWindow":120}'
510	```
511	
512	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
513	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no alert is
514	  written.
515	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
516	  blank or non-string identifiers, booleans/floats where integers are
517	  required, non-positive values, unpaired `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
518	
519	### `GET /alerts?organizationId=...`
520	
521	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
522	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "alerts": [...]}`
523	containing only that organization's alerts. Each entry carries `alertId`,
524	`type`, `peakStart`, `threshold`, and `suppressedCount`, sorted by
525	`peakStart` ascending and then `alertId` in Unicode code-point order. An
526	unknown organization returns `"alerts": []`. A missing, blank, or
527	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
528	
529	## Snapshots and branches
530	
531	Snapshots capture the current main service state under a unique name so that
532	decisions can later be recomputed against that exact state. Branches fork a
533	snapshot into an isolated copy that supports the existing event, aggregate,
534	decision, and reservation entry points without sharing any mutable state with
535	the main service or with other branches.
536	
537	### Organization boundaries
538	
539	Every snapshot and branch is owned by the organization of the `write`
540	credential that created it, and all capture, naming, and visibility rules are
541	scoped to that boundary:
542	
543	- A snapshot captures **only the creator's own organization** — its events,
544	  the capacities of resources it reserves, and its reservations. Other
545	  organizations' events, reservation identifiers, and capacity records are
546	  neither captured nor summarized. The three counts in the response
547	  (`events`, `resources`, `reservations`) count only that organization. Two
548	  snapshots created from the same state return identical counts; another
549	  organization's data never changes them.
550	- A branch forked from a snapshot carries only that snapshot organization's
551	  data. Inside the branch, event and reservation names are compared only
552	  against that organization's own records. Another organization's event
553	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never cause a
554	  branch commit to conflict and never affect a branch balance.
555	- Snapshot and branch names are **unique across the whole service** and are
556	  owned by the creator's organization. A duplicate name conflicts regardless
557	  of which organization holds it: creating a snapshot with a name already in
558	  use returns `409` `snapshot_conflict` (the original snapshot is never
559	  rewritten), and creating a branch with a name already in use returns `409`
560	  `branch_conflict` (the existing branch is untouched). Names are not
561	  namespaced per organization.
562	- Using another organization's **snapshot name as a fork source**, or reading
563	  another organization's **branch by name**, returns `403 Forbidden`
564	  (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) with no content, even though the name exists. A
565	  name that has never appeared anywhere is the only case that yields `404`:
566	  a missing snapshot is `snapshot_not_found` and a missing branch is
567	  `branch_not_found`. Missing objects are never implicitly created.
568	- When creating a branch, snapshot ownership (`403`) is decided before the
569	  duplicate branch name (`409`); a foreign snapshot is forbidden even if the
570	  requested `branchId` is also taken. The snapshot list (`GET /snapshots`)
571	  and branch summaries are visible only within the owning organization.
572	- Authorization and the write happen under one lock for alert evaluation,
573	  snapshot creation, and branch creation alike. A rejected request leaves no
574	  alert, snapshot, or branch behind, and concurrent creations of the same
575	  name have exactly one winner; the loser receives the conflict response.
576	
577	Snapshots and branches capture only events, resource capacities, and
578	reservations — alerts are never captured, and the alert entry points remain
579	main-only with no branch-prefixed sub-paths. Like everything else here,
580	snapshots and branches live only in the server process and are cleared on
581	restart; there is no persistence, authorization, or replay across restarts.
582	
583	### `POST /snapshots`
584	
585	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
586	must be a JSON object containing exactly one field:
587	
588	| Field        | Rule                     |
589	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
590	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
591	
592	The snapshot is owned by the caller's organization and captures only that
593	organization's state. A successful response is `201` with compact integer
594	JSON and one trailing newline, matching the byte contract of the other write
595	entry points:
596	
597	```json
598	{"events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
599	```
600	
601	- `events`, `resources`, and `reservations` count the creator organization's
602	  captured events, distinct resources with a recorded capacity, and
603	  reservations; other organizations' data is never counted.
604	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "snapshot_conflict"}`) — the name already exists
605	  anywhere in the service (held by any organization); the original snapshot
606	  content is never replaced or mutated.
607	- `403 Forbidden` — the credential is read-only or acts outside its
608	  organization; no snapshot is stored.
609	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
610	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
611	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, a missing or extra field,
612	  a blank value, or a non-string `snapshotId`.
613	- Any failed request leaves both the main state and existing snapshots
614	  unchanged.
615	
616	### `GET /snapshots`
617	
618	Returns `200` with `{"snapshots": [...]}`, listing **only the caller
619	organization's** snapshots; other organizations' snapshots are never visible.
620	Each entry has the same shape as a creation response, and entries are sorted
621	by `snapshotId` in Unicode code-point order. With no snapshots the collection
622	is an empty array.
623	
624	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources?organizationId=...`
625	
626	A read-only listing of one snapshot's captured resource balances for the
627	caller's organization — the single-snapshot counterpart of
628	`POST /snapshots/compare/resources`, computed from the exact same balance
629	contract. Snapshots are immutable, so nothing in the snapshot, in any branch,
630	or in the main service is read for mutation or written: the main-service
631	event ledger, reservation inventory, and alert state are untouched, failed
632	requests leave no trace, and identical requests return byte-for-byte
633	identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials may call it. The
634	`organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
635	
636	The `200` response echoes the organization and snapshot identifiers and
637	carries one row per resource the organization reserves in the snapshot,
638	sorted by `resourceId` in Unicode code-point order. Each row reports the
639	three balances: `capacity` (fixed by the first captured reservation naming
640	the resource), `occupied` (the sum of every captured reservation the
641	organization holds against the resource — multiple reservations all count),
642	and `remaining` (`capacity - occupied`). Reservations of other
643	organizations never contribute (they are never captured), and a snapshot
644	with no resources returns an empty `resources` array. Because the balances
645	share the comparison's contract, comparing a snapshot with itself via
646	`POST /snapshots/compare/resources` reports every listed row as `equal`,
647	item by item.
648	
649	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
650	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
651	
652	```json
653	{"organizationId":"org-1","resources":[{"capacity":10,"occupied":3,"remaining":7,"resourceId":"res-a"},{"capacity":4,"occupied":1,"remaining":3,"resourceId":"res-b"}],"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
654	```
655	
656	```bash
657	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/snap-1/resources?organizationId=org-1' \
658	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
659	```
660	
661	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
662	query shape, then the organization, and only then the snapshot name.
663	
664	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
665	  is missing, malformed, or not registered.
666	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — the `organizationId`
667	  parameter is missing, duplicated, or blank.
668	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
669	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named snapshot
670	  belongs to another organization.
671	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — the snapshot name
672	  has never existed; a listing never implicitly creates a snapshot.
673	
674	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
675	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
676	
677	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/reservations?organizationId=...`
678	
679	A read-only listing of one snapshot's captured reservations for the
680	caller's organization — the single-snapshot counterpart of
681	`POST /snapshots/compare/reservations`, computed from the exact same
682	captured-reservation contract. Snapshots are immutable, so nothing in the
683	snapshot, in any branch, or in the main service is read for mutation or
684	written: the main-service event ledger, reservation inventory, and alert
685	state are untouched, failed requests leave no trace, and identical
686	requests return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
687	credentials may call it. The `organizationId` query parameter must appear
688	exactly once and be non-empty.
689	
690	The `200` response echoes the organization and snapshot identifiers and
691	carries one row per reservation captured in the snapshot, sorted by
692	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each row
693	reports exactly the five reservation fields the reservation comparison
694	aligns on: `organizationId`, `reservationId`, `resourceId`, `quantity`,
695	and `capacity`. Reservations of other organizations never contribute
696	(they are never captured), and a snapshot with no reservations returns an
697	empty `reservations` array. Because the rows share the comparison's
698	contract, comparing a snapshot with itself via
699	`POST /snapshots/compare/reservations` lists every reservation in `same`
700	with zero diffs, item by item.
701	
702	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
703	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
704	
705	```json
706	{"organizationId":"org-1","reservations":[{"capacity":10,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"res-a"}],"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
707	```
708	
709	```bash
710	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/snap-1/reservations?organizationId=org-1' \
711	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
712	```
713	
714	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
715	query shape, then the organization, and only then the snapshot name.
716	
717	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
718	  is missing, malformed, or not registered.
719	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — the `organizationId`
720	  parameter is missing, duplicated, or blank.
721	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
722	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named snapshot
723	  belongs to another organization.
724	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — the snapshot name
725	  has never existed; a listing never implicitly creates a snapshot.
726	
727	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
728	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
729	
730	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events?organizationId=...`
731	
732	A read-only listing of one snapshot's captured events for the caller's
733	organization — the single-snapshot counterpart of
734	`POST /snapshots/compare/events`, built from the exact same captured-event

1003	### Branch-prefixed entry points
1004	
1005	A known branch exposes the existing endpoints under
1006	`/branches/{branchId}/...`, with identical request contracts, query
1007	validation, ordering, and window semantics:
1008	
1009	| Method | Path                                      | Effect                                    |
1010	| ------ | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
1011	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | list the branch's events                  |
1012	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events/aggregate`   | aggregate the branch's events             |
1013	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | commit an event into the branch only      |
1014	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/decisions/evaluate` | evaluate against the branch's events only |
1015	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | list the branch's reservations            |
1016	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/resources`          | list the branch's resource balances       |
1017	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | reserve against branch balances only      |

1020	  and `event_id_conflict` (`409`); writes stay in the branch. Name and
1021	  capacity comparisons run only against the owning organization's records
1022	  that were forked into the branch, so another organization's event
1023	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never trigger a
1024	  conflict and never affect a branch balance.

1026	  capacity rules: identical replays return `200` without double counting,

1028	  `capacity_exceeded` still return `409`; a failed commit never changes the

1031	  main endpoints; missing, duplicated, or empty parameters return `422` with

1037	  never observe each other's writes. Unknown sub-paths under a known branch

1095	### `POST /branches/compare`
1096	
1097	A read-only comparison of two existing branches' window counts and peak
1098	decisions. Each side recomputes its window counts and peak from that
1099	branch's own events only; nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or
1100	in the main service is read for mutation or written, and identical
1101	submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
1102	credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a
1103	Bearer credential bound to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be
1104	a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
1105	
1106	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1107	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1108	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
1109	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
1110	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
1111	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
1112	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1113	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1114	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
1115	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
1116	
1117	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1118	are then equal by construction. Window division matches the aggregate and
1119	decision entry points exactly: windows start at `0` and cover
1120	`[start, start + windowSize)`, and an event counts toward the window of
1121	`floor(occurredAt / windowSize) * windowSize`.
1122	
1123	- Without `from`/`to`, the `windows` rows cover the **union** of the windows
1124	  hit by matching events on either side, aligned row-by-row by `start`
1125	  ascending. A window hit by only one side shows the other side's count as
1126	  `0`. When neither side has a matching event, `windows` is `[]`.
1127	- With `from`/`to`, only events in the closed interval
1128	  `from <= occurredAt <= to` count, and **every** window intersecting that
1129	  interval gets a row, including windows empty on both sides.
1130	- Each row is `{"start", "leftCount", "rightCount", "equal"}`, with
1131	  `equal` true exactly when the two counts agree.
1132	- `decision.left` and `decision.right` each carry `peakStart`,
1133	  `peakCount`, and `action`: the peak is the largest window count, ties
1134	  resolve to the earliest window start, and `action` is `"escalate"` when
1135	  the peak reaches `threshold` and `"observe"` otherwise. `decision.equal`
1136	  is true exactly when the two sides' peak results agree. An empty side has
1137	  `peakStart: null`, `peakCount: 0`, and `action: "observe"`.
1138	
1139	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1140	values kept as integers, booleans kept as booleans, and one trailing
1141	newline:
1142	
1143	```json
1144	{"decision":{"equal":false,"left":{"action":"observe","peakCount":2,"peakStart":0},"right":{"action":"escalate","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60}},"from":null,"left":"br-a","organizationId":"org-1","right":"br-b","threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"windows":[{"equal":false,"leftCount":2,"rightCount":1,"start":0},{"equal":false,"leftCount":0,"rightCount":3,"start":60}]}
1145	```
1146	
1147	```bash
1148	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare \
1149	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1150	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1151	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
1152	```
1153	
1154	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
1155	  registered.
1156	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
1157	  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
1158	  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
1159	  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
1160	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
1161	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
1162	  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
1163	  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
1164	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1165	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1166	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1167	  missing or extra field, a blank or non-string `organizationId`/`left`/
1168	  `right`/`type`, non-positive-integer `windowSize`/`threshold`, unpaired or
1169	  non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
1170	
1171	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1172	branch and changes no event, reservation, or decision state.

1174	### `POST /branches/compare/events`
1175	
1176	A read-only, event-level comparison of two existing branches. Where
1177	`POST /branches/compare` aligns window counts, this entry point aligns the
1178	two branches' events by `eventId` and reports the deterministic difference
1179	summary. Nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or in the main
1180	service is read for mutation or written, and identical submissions return
1181	byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials may call
1182	it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a Bearer credential bound
1183	to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object
1184	containing exactly these fields:
1185	
1186	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1187	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1188	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
1189	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
1190	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
1191	
1192	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1193	are then equal by construction and every shared event lands in `same`.
1194	
1195	Events are aligned by `eventId`:
1196	
1197	- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left branch.
1198	- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right branch.
1199	- `same` — identifiers on both sides whose events are identical in every
1200	  field except `eventId`; payloads compare by content, so key order inside
1201	  a payload never matters.
1202	- `diff` — identifiers on both sides whose events disagree. Each entry is
1203	  `{"eventId", "fields"}`, where `fields` names the mismatched fields
1204	  (drawn from `organizationId`, `type`, `occurredAt`, `payload`).
1205	
1206	Identifiers and field names are sorted in Unicode code-point order. Each
1207	group array is accompanied by a count key named after the group plus
1208	`Count` (`leftOnlyCount`, `rightOnlyCount`, `sameCount`, `diffCount`). When
1209	neither branch holds any event, all four groups are empty arrays and all
1210	four counts are `0`.
1211	
1212	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1213	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
1214	
1215	```json
1216	{"diff":[{"eventId":"evt-2","fields":["occurredAt","payload"]}],"diffCount":1,"leftOnly":["evt-1"],"leftOnlyCount":1,"rightOnly":["evt-4"],"rightOnlyCount":1,"same":["evt-3"],"sameCount":1}
1217	```
1218	
1219	```bash
1220	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare/events \
1221	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1222	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1223	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b"}'
1224	```
1225	
1226	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
1227	  registered.
1228	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
1229	  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
1230	  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
1231	  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
1232	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
1233	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
1234	  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
1235	  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
1236	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1237	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1238	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1239	  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
1240	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
1241	
1242	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1243	branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1244	
1245	### `POST /branches/compare/reservations`
1246	
1247	A read-only, reservation-level comparison of two existing branches. Where
1248	`POST /branches/compare/events` aligns events by `eventId`, this entry point
1249	aligns the two branches' reservations by `reservationId` and reports the
1250	deterministic difference summary. Nothing in either branch, in any other
1251	branch, or in the main service is read for mutation or written, alert state
1252	is untouched, and identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
1253	Both `read` and `write` credentials may call it. Requires
1254	`Content-Type: application/json` and a Bearer credential bound to the
1255	request's `organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object containing
1256	exactly these fields:
1257	
1258	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1259	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1260	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
1261	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
1262	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
1263	
1264	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1265	are then equal by construction and every shared reservation lands in
1266	`same`.
1267	
1268	Reservations are aligned by `reservationId`:
1269	
1270	- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left branch.
1271	- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right branch.
1272	- `same` — identifiers on both sides whose `organizationId`, `resourceId`,
1273	  `quantity`, and `capacity` all match.
1274	- `diff` — identifiers on both sides that disagree in at least one of those
1275	  four fields. Each entry is `{"reservationId", "fields"}`, where `fields`
1276	  names the mismatched fields, drawn only from `organizationId`,
1277	  `resourceId`, `quantity`, and `capacity`; no other content participates
1278	  in the comparison.
1279	
1280	Identifiers and field names are sorted in Unicode code-point order. Each
1281	group array is accompanied by a count key named after the group plus
1282	`Count` (`leftOnlyCount`, `rightOnlyCount`, `sameCount`, `diffCount`). When
1283	neither branch holds any reservation for the organization, all four groups
1284	are empty arrays and all four counts are `0`.
1285	
1286	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1287	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
1288	
1289	```json
1290	{"diff":[{"fields":["capacity","quantity"],"reservationId":"res-2"}],"diffCount":1,"leftOnly":["res-1"],"leftOnlyCount":1,"rightOnly":["res-4"],"rightOnlyCount":1,"same":["res-3"],"sameCount":1}
1291	```
1292	
1293	```bash
1294	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare/reservations \
1295	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1296	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1297	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b"}'
1298	```
1299	
1300	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
1301	  registered.
1302	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
1303	  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
1304	  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
1305	  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
1306	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
1307	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
1308	  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
1309	  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
1310	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1311	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1312	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1313	  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
1314	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
1315	
1316	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1317	branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1318	
1319	### `POST /branches/compare/resources`
1320	
1321	A read-only, resource-balance comparison of two existing branches. Where
1322	`POST /branches/compare/reservations` aligns reservations by
1323	`reservationId`, this entry point aligns the two branches' resources by
1324	`resourceId` and compares each resource's three balances — `capacity`,
1325	`occupied`, and `remaining` — as they currently stand in the branches.
1326	Nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or in the main service is
1327	read for mutation or written, alert state is untouched, and identical
1328	submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
1329	credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a
1330	Bearer credential bound to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be
1331	a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
1332	
1333	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1334	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1335	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
1336	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
1337	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
1338	
1339	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1340	are then the same branch and every row's `equal` marker is true.
1341	
1342	Resources are aligned by `resourceId`. The `resources` array carries one row
1343	per resource in the union of the two sides, sorted by `resourceId` in
1344	Unicode code-point order. Each row is
1345	`{"resourceId", "left", "right", "equal"}`, where `left` and `right` each
1346	hold the three balances `capacity`, `occupied`, and `remaining`. A resource
1347	missing on one side is treated as absent and that side's three balances are
1348	all `0`. `equal` is true exactly when the two sides' three balances all
1349	agree, and false when any one of them differs.
1350	
1351	In addition to the rows, four grouping arrays partition the resources:
1352	
1353	- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left branch.
1354	- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right branch.
1355	- `same` — identifiers present on both sides whose `capacity`, `occupied`,
1356	  and `remaining` all match.
